about: Stack budgets read by src/iot/tools/stack_budget.py (ESPR-4). A ratchet: each number is what the code used when it was set, lowered as the code shrinks and raised only in the commit that needs it, with the reason. `goal` is where the 2026-11-13 analysis says the bridge should be on its 4 KB cont stack (an interrupt adds >= 256 B at peak); the gate runs loop() on an 8 KB task stack. The path budget carries 48 B over the measured path for toolchain variance between hosts; frames carry none. The ESP32's GCC 8 cannot write a call graph, so the gate has no path budget.

court_bridge.lowered: Bridge 3.1.0 moved the lifeline (OTA, persistence, supervisor) out of loop()'s own frame into functions called from its top, and the heartbeat/reply/RSA buffers into one static: loop()'s frame went 928 -> 208 B and the deepest path 3,136 -> 2,608 B, so both budgets were lowered with it.

door_gate.raised: Gate 2.0.0's network adoption (devnet::adoptNet: a staged NetSet and the base URL decoded with headroom) is an 832 B frame. The integration first took the 2.0.0 gate from 3,904 B down to this by moving every whole-image temporary off the stack; the gate's loop task is 8 KB and its worst path, measured with the analysis's call-graph tool, is 4,576 B of the 6,000 B the contract allows (device-api.md section 13).
